evidence: The callback chain is as described: receivers.py:219 defers `products.stamphog.backend.facade.api.queue_inbox_pr_review`, and facade/api.py:147 defers `products.stamphog.backend.tasks.tasks.process_inbox_pr_review`; tasks/tasks.py:27-30 imports StamphogGitHubClient (logic/github_client.py:20-27: jwt, requests, egress transport) and execute_stamphog_review_workflow (temporal/client.py:13-15: temporalio.common + posthog.temporal.common.client) at module scope. The deferral is deliberate, not a cycle: receivers.py:41-42 and facade/api.py:144-146 keep the facade off the django.setup() path because review_hog's API serializer imports it. But the cost the finding attributes to this save path is already paid, pre-fork, by every web process: posthog/urls.py:74 imports `products.stamphog.backend.facade.webhooks` at module scope, facade/webhooks.py:7 imports presentation/webhooks.py at module scope, and presentation/webhooks.py:18 imports `products.stamphog.backend.tasks.tasks` at module scope; posthog/wsgi.py:33-44 resolves the full URLconf at module load in the prototype process (`get_resolver().url_patterns`) so it lands in the gc.freeze()d copy-on-write heap, and test_startup_import_budget.py:441-447 enforces that the wsgi import resolves the URLconf. So by the time any request-thread TaskRun save (tasks API partial_update/set_output at presentation/views/api.py:1082/1107, or the webhook backstop) reaches the on_commit callback (receivers.py:130-139), tasks.tasks is in sys.modules and the deferred import is a dict lookup with zero added retention. The '~0.6 s clean post-setup import' was measured against a bare django.setup(), which is not the web process's state. No repo guard is violated: FORBIDDEN_AT_SETUP (test_startup_import_budget.py:12-43) snapshots a bare django.setup() only, and receivers.py:44-53 imports only the light inbox_hooks module at top, so tasks.tasks stays off setup. Non-web savers (Temporal task workers writing output.pr_url via process_task/workflow.py:607-640) already have temporalio loaded and are 'background workers paying lazily', which docs/internal/django-startup-time.md:197-198 calls fine. The sibling `_start_review` in the same callback (receivers.py:243-257) defers the heavier `products.review_hog.backend.temporal.client` (temporal/__init__.py:1-25 registers every activity; client.py:24-30 pulls temporalio + PRParser) on the same save path, so the stamphog branch duplicates an existing, documented pattern rather than introducing a new class of cost. `send_task` by name (precedent: customer_analytics/backend/facade/api.py:1121-1124) would work since process_inbox_pr_review declares no queue (tasks.py:1109), but it buys nothing here and trades a checked import for a free-floating task-name string.
notes: Would become a `consider` if posthog/urls.py stopped importing stamphog_github_webhook eagerly (lazy view string) or posthog/wsgi.py dropped the URLconf pre-warm, since then the first opted-in TaskRun save per web worker would pay the import on a request thread; even then it is one-time, toggle-gated, inside an on_commit callback that already performs a broker publish, and smaller than the sibling review_hog Temporal import on the same path. Would become should_fix only if a measured request-path stall were shown in a real web process after those preconditions changed.
